title: Tech Graphics: Illustration Style
request: Oct 18 2026 22:30 ICT: decks for the graphics of the technicians (how techs are illustrated in the investor pitch and brand graphics, not the tech app); drawn SVG mockups only; fixed picks from the earlier uniform decks drawn in, not re-asked
note: Oct 18 2026 22:30 ICT request: drawing approach for the illustrated techs (shading, outline, crop, proportions, faces, hero vs pair, pose, backdrop, set variety, line weight)
fixed_picks: Drawn in, not asked: illustrated people only; healthy, fit young adults with varied builds; left-chest logo, big back wordmark, printed first name, white cap with front mark, long charcoal pants, plain black belt, sneakers for good weather and boots for bad weather, terracotta reusable logo shoe covers always visible, charcoal softshell for cold days.
example_data: Every card is a hand-built SVG mockup of an illustrated tech (round-2 pitch figure style); sample first name only; nothing live is changed.
built_at_note: Tech graphics decks Oct 18 2026 22:30 ICT request

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Shading, should the techs be drawn as flat vector shapes or soft-shaded vector with gentle light and shadow?

optionA.label: Flat Vector
optionA.desc: Solid colour shapes, no gradients; crisp at any size.

optionB.label: Soft-Shaded Vector
optionB.desc: Same shapes with gentle side light, shadow and fabric shading.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Outline, should each tech be drawn with no outline or with a dark ink outline around every shape?

optionA.label: No Outline
optionA.desc: Shapes meet colour to colour, like the round-2 pitch.

optionB.label: Ink Outline
optionB.desc: A dark line around the body, clothes and gear.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Crop, should a tech graphic show the full figure head to toe or a three-quarter crop with the shoe covers in an inset?

optionA.label: Full Figure
optionA.desc: Head to shoe covers, the whole uniform in one view.

optionB.label: Three-Quarter Crop
optionB.desc: Head to knee, bigger and closer; covers shown in a corner inset.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Body proportions, should techs keep realistic adult proportions or a slightly stylized look with a larger head?

optionA.label: Realistic Proportions
optionA.desc: About seven and a half heads tall, like a real fit adult.

optionB.label: Slightly Stylized
optionB.desc: Head about a third bigger; friendlier, more character-like.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Faces, should techs have simple faces with eyes, brows and a smile or be faceless with hair and ears only?

optionA.label: Simple Faces
optionA.desc: Dot eyes, brows, a small nose line and a smile.

optionB.label: Faceless
optionB.desc: Skin, ears and hair only, no features drawn.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: How many techs, should the main tech graphic show one tech as the hero or a pair of techs side by side?

optionA.label: One Tech Hero
optionA.desc: A single tech, centred and larger.

optionB.label: A Pair
optionB.desc: Two techs side by side, good-weather and bad-weather kit.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Pose, should techs stand in a calm static pose or be shown mid-task, here sliding a fresh filter into a furnace?

optionB.label: Mid-Task
optionB.desc: Gloved hands sliding a fresh filter into the furnace slot.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Backdrop, should a tech sit on plain warm cream or in front of a light room scene with a window, wall and floor?

optionA.label: Plain Cream
optionA.desc: Just the tech and a soft floor shadow on cream.

optionB.label: Light Room Scene
optionB.desc: Pale wall, window, thermostat and a wood floor behind.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Skin tone and build variety, should the brand set show four techs with a range of skin tones and builds or a set of two?

optionA.label: A Set Of Four
optionA.desc: Four techs, four skin tones, broad to slim-athletic builds.

optionB.label: A Set Of Two
optionB.desc: Two techs with different tones and builds.

pairs.ask: Smart Upkeep Tech Graphics: Line weight, where outlines are used should they be a thin fine line or a medium line that holds up when the graphic is small?

optionA.label: Thin Line
optionA.desc: A fine dark line, about half a point at phone size.

optionB.label: Medium Line
optionB.desc: A firmer line, about twice as thick.
